newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's July oil trade deficit narrows 11.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Peru's July oil trade deficit narrows 11.1 pct.

text.p: Peru's oil and derivatives trade deficit narrowed 11.1 percent to $24 million, compared with the same month last year, the Central Reserve Bank said Monday.
The oil and derivatives deficit rose 10.3 percent in the first seven months of the year to $172 million, compared with same period last year, the bank said.
July's imports of oil and derivatives were $50 million, up from $49 million in the same month last year. Exports in July rose to $26 million from $22 million in the same month last year.
In the first seven months of the year, imports of oil and derivatives rose 32 percent to $384 million. Exports rose 56 percent to $212 million, compared with the same period in 1995.
Peru's oil deficit swelled 134 percent to $323.2 million in 1995 compared with $138 million the previous year, according to the Energy and Mines Ministry.
